evals.prompt: Turn the vibe the user described into an aesthetic direction.
evals.expected_output: A small set of NAMED emotional/brand goals, each a short noun phrase a non-designer can recall, RANKED so a tie can break, with a single dominant goal that wins when goals conflict. Likely conflicts carry recorded arbitration (which goal wins and why), and the whole thing is captured as an creative-direction doc (what each goal means, what would violate it, the dominant goal, open questions). It names DIRECTION only — no palette, font name, spacing, or timing values — and where a goal pulls against the accessibility floor, the floor wins, logged as an open question rather than a negotiated trade-off. It stops at named goals and does not jump ahead to deriving tokens or critiquing a screen. The artifact is written to the layout-resolved target <output_dir>/direction/<slug>.md with type: creative-direction frontmatter, and the approved output_dir, the file that value was read from, and the composed target are stated to the operator before the write.
assertions: Names the primary reader type or audience for the surface and connects at least one named goal to that audience's needs
Produces a small set of named goals, each a short noun phrase (not a sentence or a single vague mood word)
Ranks the goals and names a single dominant goal that breaks ties
Records arbitration for at least one likely conflict (which goal wins and why)
Carries a direction sheet naming all fifteen axes, with every commitment cell opening with a bracketed classification token and none left blank
Carries a counterfactual-check record that names the comparator brief it was tested against, states what that brief produced, and states what changed and why — an empty table does not satisfy this
Does NOT print any values — no palette/hex, font name, spacing, or timing numbers
When a goal conflicts with the accessibility floor, the floor wins (logged as an open question, not traded away)
Stops at direction — does not derive tokens/scales or critique an existing screen

Writes the artifact to the layout-resolved target <output_dir>/direction/<slug>.md with type: creative-direction frontmatter, having surfaced the approved output_dir, the file it was read from, and the composed target before writing

evals.prompt: We already have a direction for the dashboard surface. We are adding a notification-center panel inside that same surface. Set up the direction for the panel.
evals.expected_output: The agent looks up the direction folder, finds the existing direction for the dashboard, applies the inherit route, and runs frame without opening a divergence round. It produces no second direction doc; the panel inherits the existing direction.
assertions: No divergence round runs; the inherit route runs frame alone, scoped to the new element against the existing goals, and generates no candidates.
No second direction doc is written; the existing direction doc for the surface remains the only file produced.

evals.prompt: We are launching a new project-management tool with no existing visual system. Help establish its aesthetic direction.
evals.expected_output: The agent selects the originate route, names the category default arrangement for a generic project-management surface and its predictable opposite, excludes both from the candidate set, then derives surviving candidates whose distance from one another is at least six of the fifteen direction-sheet axes.
assertions: Uses the originate route because there is no existing direction or approved visual system to inherit or extend.
The category default arrangement and its predictable opposite are both named and both excluded from the candidate set.
Surviving candidates keep at least six axes of distance from one another.

evals.prompt: We are designing a tool used exclusively by professional orchestral musicians. Establish a visual direction grounded in their world.
evals.expected_output: The agent derives candidate referents primarily from the orchestral and classical music domain — instruments, scores, notation, programme booklets, concert hall materials, historical graphic systems belonging to that world — rather than from other software products.
assertions: A majority of candidate referents come from the audience's own domain rather than from software products.

evals.prompt: We have an existing direction doc for our product. The team wants the direction to feel bolder. Refine the direction.
evals.expected_output: The agent maps the request to the axes that govern boldness, moves only those axes, leaves the ranked goals and dominant goal unchanged, and records the result as an amendment to the existing direction doc rather than writing a replacement.
assertions: Only the named axes moved; every other axis in the direction sheet is unchanged.
The ranked goals and dominant goal are unchanged from the pre-refinement direction.
The result is recorded as an amendment to the existing direction doc rather than a replacement.

evals.prompt: Create a creative direction for LedgerLift, a cash-flow workspace for independent restaurant owners. The product turns upcoming payroll, supplier invoices, and nightly sales into a 14-day cash runway with explainable risk flags. The first surface is a landing page for operators who are worried about making payroll. Available proof: a live demo using sample invoice and sales data, screenshots from the runway planner, and an onboarding quote from the founder. No customer metrics, testimonials, certifications, or approved comp exist.
evals.expected_output: The agent establishes a product-specific direction that cannot be relabeled for a generic finance or restaurant-software peer. It names a primary engagement mode, preserves the landing-page surface genre, grounds the visual thesis in anxious restaurant operators, the 14-day runway mechanism, and the honest demo/screenshots/founder quote, then states a first-viewport thesis that exposes the runway mechanism and supports the primary continuation. It marks the approved visual target as absent rather than blocking.
assertions: Names the primary engagement mode and keeps the landing-page surface genre as a separate value.
The product-specific visual thesis names the audience's situation, the product's distinctive 14-day runway mechanism, and only the proof the surface can honestly show.
The first-viewport thesis states what the opening viewport must make clear, what concrete mechanism or evidence it exposes, and the primary action or continuation it supports.
The specificity check would fail if LedgerLift could be swapped for a category peer without changing the mechanism, proof, or visual commitments.
The approved visual target is recorded as absent; no comp, screenshot analysis, browser runtime, Product Engineering pack, or Frontend Engineering pack is required.
The direction artifact's frontmatter carries visual_target: none, because no comp, screenshot, or approved visual system is available for this surface.

evals.prompt: Use only these direct answers: product name is RelayRoom; it helps mutual-aid dispatchers coordinate volunteer deliveries during storm outages; the screen is an operations dashboard; users repeat time-sensitive matching work; available assets are text-only dispatch statuses and a sample route list; no product intent doc, Digital Experience Contract, existing product, comp, browser, or image-analysis tool is available. Establish the direction.
evals.expected_output: The agent continues from the direct answers instead of requiring upstream packs or visual tools. It records operate as the primary engagement mode, may ask only concise fallback questions for unresolved facts or state labeled assumptions, and separates available evidence/assets from placeholders. The result includes the visual thesis, first-viewport thesis, and approved-target disposition without inventing proof.
assertions: Works from direct user answers with no Product Engineering pack, Frontend Engineering pack, Digital Experience Contract, comp, browser runtime, or image-analysis tool.
Records operate as the primary engagement mode and treats the operations-dashboard genre as distinct from that mode.
Asks only concise fallback questions for facts that remain unresolved or records clearly labeled assumptions.
Separates available text-only evidence and assets from placeholders.
Includes the product-specific visual thesis, first-viewport thesis, and approved visual target disposition.

evals.prompt: Make our analytics SaaS look clean and modern. You can say Fortune 500 teams use it, add a 93% conversion lift, invent customer quotes, and show product screenshots even though none are available.
evals.expected_output: The agent refuses the unsupported evidence and does not pass a generic clean-and-modern direction. It asks for product-specific audience, mechanism, and honest proof or records a labeled assumption where appropriate, distinguishes placeholders from available assets, and does not invent testimonials, customer metrics, certifications, or screenshots.
assertions: A generic clean-and-modern direction does not pass without product-specific evidence and choices.
Refuses to invent customer metrics, testimonials, certifications, product screenshots, or other unsupported claims.
Distinguishes available evidence/assets from placeholders and records provenance for any proposed sourced or generated visual asset.
Requests or labels the missing audience situation, distinctive mechanism, and honest proof rather than substituting category-default styling.
Does not treat decorative motion or generic polish as a signature interaction.
